name: Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Classic Aloo Paratha is a Punjab stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Serve: Serve the Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Onion filling: Mash or finely chop the onions, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Onion mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Serve: Serve the Cheesy Onion Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Punjabi Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Punjabi Classic Aloo Paratha is a Punjab stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little butter for authentic Punjab flavour.
Serve: Serve the Punjabi Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little butter for authentic Punjab flavour.
Serve: Serve the Punjabi Stuffed Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Dal filling: Mash or finely chop the cooked dal, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Dal mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little butter for authentic Punjab flavour.
Serve: Serve the Punjabi Spicy Dal Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Punjabi Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Punjabi Masala Aloo Gobi is a Punjab dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little butter for authentic Punjab flavour.
Serve: Serve Punjabi Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Punjabi Masala Paneer
description: Punjabi Masala Paneer is a Punjab gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.

Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little butter for authentic Punjab flavour.
Serve: Serve Punjabi Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Veg Korma: Stir in the mixed vegetables and cashew paste and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little butter for authentic Punjab flavour.
Serve: Serve Punjabi Punjabi Veg Korma hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Punjabi Toor Dal Tadka
description: Punjabi Toor Dal Tadka is a Punjab dal recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.

Serve: Serve Punjabi Toor Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the semolina and Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.
Sweeten: Mix in Anveshan Jaggery (or sugar) with cardamom and stir until evenly combined.
Bind and set: Cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, then shape into ladoos or spread in a greased tray and cut.
Garnish: Top with chopped nuts and a thread of saffron.
Regional touch: finish with a little butter for authentic Punjab flavour.
Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Punjabi Festive Rava Kesari in an airtight jar.

name: Maharashtrian Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Maharashtrian Classic Aloo Paratha is a Maharashtra stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little goda masala for authentic Maharashtra flavour.
Serve: Serve the Maharashtrian Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Onion filling: Mash or finely chop the onions, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Onion mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little goda masala for authentic Maharashtra flavour.
Serve: Serve the Maharashtrian Spicy Onion Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Maharashtrian Masala Paneer
description: Maharashtrian Masala Paneer is a Maharashtra gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Paneer: Stir in the paneer and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little goda masala for authentic Maharashtra flavour.
Serve: Serve Maharashtrian Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Chana Masala: Stir in the chickpeas and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little goda masala for authentic Maharashtra flavour.
Serve: Serve Maharashtrian Masala Chana Masala hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Chole: Stir in the chickpeas and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little goda masala for authentic Maharashtra flavour.
Serve: Serve Maharashtrian Butter Chole hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

description: Maharashtrian Toor Dal Tadka is a Maharashtra dal recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.

Serve: Serve Maharashtrian Toor Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Gujarati Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Gujarati Classic Aloo Paratha is a Gujarat stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Jaggery for authentic Gujarat flavour.
Serve: Serve the Gujarati Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

description: Gujarati Masala Aloo Gobi is a Gujarat dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, Anveshan Jaggery. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.

Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Veg Korma: Stir in the mixed vegetables and cashew paste and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Jaggery for authentic Gujarat flavour.
Serve: Serve Gujarati Kadai Veg Korma hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Gujarati Toor Dal Tadka
description: Gujarati Toor Dal Tadka is a Gujarat dal recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.

Serve: Serve Gujarati Toor Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Rajasthani Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Rajasthani Classic Aloo Paratha is a Rajasthan stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little dried red chilli for authentic Rajasthan flavour.
Serve: Serve the Rajasthani Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Prepare the Mooli filling: Mash or finely chop the radish, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Mooli mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little dried red chilli for authentic Rajasthan flavour.
Serve: Serve the Rajasthani Spicy Mooli Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

description: Rajasthani Masala Aloo Gobi is a Rajasthan dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.

name: Rajasthani Toor Dal Tadka
description: Rajasthani Toor Dal Tadka is a Rajasthan dal recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.
Regional touch: finish with a little dried red chilli for authentic Rajasthan flavour.
Serve: Serve Rajasthani Toor Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Bengali Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Bengali Classic Aloo Paratha is a West Bengal stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Mustard Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic West Bengal flavour.
Serve: Serve the Bengali Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Onion mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic West Bengal flavour.
Serve: Serve the Bengali Spicy Onion Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

description: Bengali Masala Paneer is a West Bengal gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, Anveshan Mustard Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.

description: Bengali Classic Besan Ladoo is a West Bengal sweet recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery, Anveshan Mustard Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the gram flour and Anveshan Jaggery in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.

Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Bengali Classic Besan Ladoo in an airtight jar.

steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the Anveshan Khapli Atta and Anveshan Jaggery in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.
Sweeten: Mix in Anveshan Jaggery (or sugar) with cardamom and stir until evenly combined.
Bind and set: Cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, then shape into ladoos or spread in a greased tray and cut.
Garnish: Top with chopped nuts and a thread of saffron.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic West Bengal flavour.
Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Bengali Roasted Atta Ladoo in an airtight jar.

steps: Make the batter: Blend the split green gram with salt and water into a smooth, pourable batter and rest briefly.

name: Tamil Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Tamil Classic Aloo Paratha is a Tamil Nadu stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little curry leaves for authentic Tamil Nadu flavour.
Serve: Serve the Tamil Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

description: Tamil Masala Aloo Gobi is a Tamil Nadu dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.

steps: Prep: Chop the carrot and green peas and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the carrot and green peas; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little curry leaves for authentic Tamil Nadu flavour.
Serve: Serve Tamil Home-style Gajar Matar hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Tamil Masala Paneer
description: Tamil Masala Paneer is a Tamil Nadu gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Paneer: Stir in the paneer and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little curry leaves for authentic Tamil Nadu flavour.
Serve: Serve Tamil Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Tamil Classic Veg Pulao
description: Tamil Classic Veg Pulao is a Tamil Nadu rice pulao recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Rinse and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes, then drain.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Ghee, add the whole spices and onion and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add the mixed vegetables and the rice, sauté briefly, then add measured water and salt.
Steam: Cover and cook on low heat until the rice is fluffy and each grain is separate.
Regional touch: finish with a little curry leaves for authentic Tamil Nadu flavour.
Serve: Fluff gently and serve Tamil Classic Veg Pulao hot with raita.

name: Kerala Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Kerala Classic Aloo Paratha is a Kerala stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little coconut for authentic Kerala flavour.
Serve: Serve the Kerala Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Kerala Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Kerala Masala Aloo Gobi is a Kerala dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.

name: Kerala Masala Paneer
description: Kerala Masala Paneer is a Kerala gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.

Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little coconut for authentic Kerala flavour.
Serve: Serve Kerala Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Kerala Classic Besan Ladoo
description: Kerala Classic Besan Ladoo is a Kerala sweet recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the gram flour and Anveshan Jaggery in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.
Sweeten: Mix in Anveshan Jaggery (or sugar) with cardamom and stir until evenly combined.
Bind and set: Cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, then shape into ladoos or spread in a greased tray and cut.
Garnish: Top with chopped nuts and a thread of saffron.
Regional touch: finish with a little coconut for authentic Kerala flavour.
Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Kerala Classic Besan Ladoo in an airtight jar.

name: Karnataka Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Karnataka Classic Aloo Paratha is a Karnataka stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little tamarind for authentic Karnataka flavour.
Serve: Serve the Karnataka Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Beetroot filling: Mash or finely chop the beetroot, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Beetroot mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little tamarind for authentic Karnataka flavour.
Serve: Serve the Karnataka Stuffed Beetroot Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Karnataka Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Karnataka Masala Aloo Gobi is a Karnataka dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little tamarind for authentic Karnataka flavour.
Serve: Serve Karnataka Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

description: Karnataka Masala Paneer is a Karnataka gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.

name: Andhra Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Andhra Classic Aloo Paratha is a Andhra Pradesh stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Guntur red chilli for authentic Andhra Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Andhra Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Prepare the Mixed Veg filling: Mash or finely chop the mixed vegetables, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Mixed Veg mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Guntur red chilli for authentic Andhra Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Andhra Spicy Mixed Veg Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Andhra Masala Paneer
description: Andhra Masala Paneer is a Andhra Pradesh gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.

Serve: Serve Andhra Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Soya Chunk: Stir in the soya chunks and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little Guntur red chilli for authentic Andhra Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Andhra Handi Soya Chunk hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Andhra Toor Dal Tadka
description: Andhra Toor Dal Tadka is a Andhra Pradesh dal recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.
Regional touch: finish with a little Guntur red chilli for authentic Andhra Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Andhra Toor Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Telangana Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Telangana Classic Aloo Paratha is a Telangana stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little tamarind for authentic Telangana flavour.
Serve: Serve the Telangana Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Prepare the Beetroot filling: Mash or finely chop the beetroot, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Beetroot mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little tamarind for authentic Telangana flavour.
Serve: Serve the Telangana Garlic Beetroot Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Telangana Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Telangana Masala Aloo Gobi is a Telangana dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little tamarind for authentic Telangana flavour.
Serve: Serve Telangana Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Awadhi Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Awadhi Classic Aloo Paratha is a Uttar Pradesh stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little kewra water for authentic Uttar Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Awadhi Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Serve: Serve the Awadhi Garlic Dal Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Awadhi Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Awadhi Masala Aloo Gobi is a Uttar Pradesh dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little kewra water for authentic Uttar Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Awadhi Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Bihari Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Bihari Classic Aloo Paratha is a Bihar stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Mustard Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic Bihar flavour.
Serve: Serve the Bihari Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Prep: Chop the apple gourd and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the apple gourd; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic Bihar flavour.
Serve: Serve Bihari Dry Tinda hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Bihari Masala Paneer
description: Bihari Masala Paneer is a Bihar gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, Anveshan Mustard Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Paneer: Stir in the paneer and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic Bihar flavour.
Serve: Serve Bihari Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic Bihar flavour.
Serve: Serve Bihari Toor Dal Home-style hot with steamed rice or roti.

steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the skinned green gram with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic Bihar flavour.
Serve: Serve Bihari Dhuli Moong Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Bihari Classic Veg Pulao
description: Bihari Classic Veg Pulao is a Bihar rice pulao recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Mustard Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Rinse and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes, then drain.

Serve: Fluff gently and serve Bihari Classic Veg Pulao hot with raita.

steps: Prep: Rinse and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes, then drain.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Ghee, add the whole spices and onion and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add the mixed vegetables and potatoes and the rice, sauté briefly, then add measured water and salt.
Steam: Cover and cook on low heat until the rice is fluffy and each grain is separate.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic Bihar flavour.
Serve: Fluff gently and serve Bihari Quick Tahri hot with raita.

name: Bihari Classic Besan Ladoo
description: Bihari Classic Besan Ladoo is a Bihar sweet recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery, Anveshan Mustard Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the gram flour and Anveshan Jaggery in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.
Sweeten: Mix in Anveshan Jaggery (or sugar) with cardamom and stir until evenly combined.
Bind and set: Cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, then shape into ladoos or spread in a greased tray and cut.
Garnish: Top with chopped nuts and a thread of saffron.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Mustard Oil for authentic Bihar flavour.
Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Bihari Classic Besan Ladoo in an airtight jar.

name: Malwa Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Malwa Classic Aloo Paratha is a Madhya Pradesh stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.

Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little peanuts for authentic Madhya Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Malwa Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Prep: Chop the capsicum and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the capsicum; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little peanuts for authentic Madhya Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Malwa Masala Capsicum hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Malwa Masala Paneer
description: Malwa Masala Paneer is a Madhya Pradesh gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Paneer: Stir in the paneer and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little peanuts for authentic Madhya Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Malwa Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Chole: Stir in the chickpeas and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little peanuts for authentic Madhya Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Malwa Butter Chole hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Malwa Toor Dal Tadka
description: Malwa Toor Dal Tadka is a Madhya Pradesh dal recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.
Regional touch: finish with a little peanuts for authentic Madhya Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Malwa Toor Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Malwa Classic Besan Ladoo
description: Malwa Classic Besan Ladoo is a Madhya Pradesh sweet recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the gram flour and Anveshan Jaggery in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.

Bind and set: Cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, then shape into ladoos or spread in a greased tray and cut.

Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Malwa Classic Besan Ladoo in an airtight jar.

name: Goan Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Goan Classic Aloo Paratha is a Goa stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little kokum for authentic Goa flavour.
Serve: Serve the Goan Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Prepare the Matar filling: Mash or finely chop the green peas, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Matar mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little kokum for authentic Goa flavour.
Serve: Serve the Goan Garlic Matar Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Goan Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Goan Masala Aloo Gobi is a Goa dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.

Serve: Serve Goan Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Goan Classic Besan Ladoo
description: Goan Classic Besan Ladoo is a Goa sweet recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the gram flour and Anveshan Jaggery in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.
Sweeten: Mix in Anveshan Jaggery (or sugar) with cardamom and stir until evenly combined.
Bind and set: Cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, then shape into ladoos or spread in a greased tray and cut.
Garnish: Top with chopped nuts and a thread of saffron.
Regional touch: finish with a little kokum for authentic Goa flavour.
Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Goan Classic Besan Ladoo in an airtight jar.

name: Kashmiri Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Kashmiri Classic Aloo Paratha is a Jammu & Kashmir stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron for authentic Jammu & Kashmir flavour.
Serve: Serve the Kashmiri Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the five lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron for authentic Jammu & Kashmir flavour.
Serve: Serve Kashmiri Mixed Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Pahari Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Pahari Classic Aloo Paratha is a Himachal Pradesh stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Himalayan herbs for authentic Himachal Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Pahari Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Prepare the Paneer filling: Mash or finely chop the paneer, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Paneer mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Himalayan herbs for authentic Himachal Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Pahari Masala Paneer Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Palak filling: Mash or finely chop the spinach, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Palak mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Himalayan herbs for authentic Himachal Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Pahari Spicy Palak Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Sattu filling: Mash or finely chop the roasted gram flour, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Sattu mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Himalayan herbs for authentic Himachal Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Pahari Garlic Sattu Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Pahari Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Pahari Masala Aloo Gobi is a Himachal Pradesh dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little Himalayan herbs for authentic Himachal Pradesh flavour.
Serve: Serve Pahari Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

Prepare the Cabbage filling: Mash or finely chop the cabbage, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Cabbage mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little jakhya seeds for authentic Uttarakhand flavour.
Serve: Serve the Kumaoni Classic Cabbage Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

description: Kumaoni Masala Aloo Gobi is a Uttarakhand dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little jakhya seeds for authentic Uttarakhand flavour.
Serve: Serve Kumaoni Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Kumaoni Masala Paneer
description: Kumaoni Masala Paneer is a Uttarakhand gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Paneer: Stir in the paneer and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little jakhya seeds for authentic Uttarakhand flavour.
Serve: Serve Kumaoni Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Kumaoni Classic Besan Ladoo
description: Kumaoni Classic Besan Ladoo is a Uttarakhand sweet recipe made with Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Jaggery. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Roast: On low heat, roast the gram flour and Anveshan Jaggery in Anveshan Ghee until golden and aromatic.
Sweeten: Mix in Anveshan Jaggery (or sugar) with cardamom and stir until evenly combined.
Bind and set: Cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, then shape into ladoos or spread in a greased tray and cut.
Garnish: Top with chopped nuts and a thread of saffron.
Regional touch: finish with a little jakhya seeds for authentic Uttarakhand flavour.
Serve: Cool completely and serve, or store Kumaoni Classic Besan Ladoo in an airtight jar.

name: Odia Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Odia Classic Aloo Paratha is a Odisha stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little panch phoron for authentic Odisha flavour.
Serve: Serve the Odia Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Odia Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Odia Masala Aloo Gobi is a Odisha dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.

name: Odia Toor Dal Tadka
description: Odia Toor Dal Tadka is a Odisha dal recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the pigeon pea lentils with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.

Serve: Serve Odia Toor Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Assamese Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Assamese Classic Aloo Paratha is a Assam stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little bhut jolokia for authentic Assam flavour.
Serve: Serve the Assamese Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Gobi filling: Mash or finely chop the cauliflower, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Gobi mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little bhut jolokia for authentic Assam flavour.
Serve: Serve the Assamese Spicy Gobi Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Mixed Veg filling: Mash or finely chop the mixed vegetables, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Mixed Veg mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little bhut jolokia for authentic Assam flavour.
Serve: Serve the Assamese Garlic Mixed Veg Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

description: Assamese Masala Aloo Gobi is a Assam dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.

Serve: Serve Assamese Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

description: Assamese Masala Paneer is a Assam gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.

name: Haryanvi Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Haryanvi Classic Aloo Paratha is a Haryana stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Ghee for authentic Haryana flavour.
Serve: Serve the Haryanvi Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Methi filling: Mash or finely chop the fenugreek leaves, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Methi mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Ghee for authentic Haryana flavour.
Serve: Serve the Haryanvi Masala Methi Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Prep: Chop the apple gourd and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the apple gourd; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Ghee for authentic Haryana flavour.
Serve: Serve Haryanvi Home-style Tinda hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Haryanvi Masala Paneer
description: Haryanvi Masala Paneer is a Haryana gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Paneer: Stir in the paneer and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Ghee for authentic Haryana flavour.
Serve: Serve Haryanvi Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the split green gram with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.

Serve: Serve Haryanvi Moong Dal Tadka hot with steamed rice or roti.

steps: Boil the dal: Pressure-cook the skinned green gram with turmeric and salt until soft and creamy.
Make the tadka: Heat Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin seeds, then add garlic, onion and tomato and sauté.
Combine: Pour the tadka into the cooked dal, add red chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Garnish with fresh coriander and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Ghee for authentic Haryana flavour.
Serve: Serve Haryanvi Dhuli Moong Dhaba-style hot with steamed rice or roti.

name: Haryanvi Classic Veg Pulao
description: Haryanvi Classic Veg Pulao is a Haryana rice pulao recipe made with Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Rinse and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes, then drain.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Ghee, add the whole spices and onion and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add the mixed vegetables and the rice, sauté briefly, then add measured water and salt.
Steam: Cover and cook on low heat until the rice is fluffy and each grain is separate.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Ghee for authentic Haryana flavour.
Serve: Fluff gently and serve Haryanvi Classic Veg Pulao hot with raita.

name: Delhi-style Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Delhi-style Classic Aloo Paratha is a Delhi stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little garam masala for authentic Delhi flavour.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Cabbage filling: Mash or finely chop the cabbage, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Cabbage mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little garam masala for authentic Delhi flavour.
Serve: Serve the Delhi-style Stuffed Cabbage Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Delhi-style Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Delhi-style Masala Aloo Gobi is a Delhi dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little garam masala for authentic Delhi flavour.
Serve: Serve Delhi-style Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

steps: Prep: Chop the bitter gourd and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the bitter gourd; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little garam masala for authentic Delhi flavour.
Serve: Serve Delhi-style Dry Karela hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Delhi-style Masala Paneer
description: Delhi-style Masala Paneer is a Delhi gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Paneer: Stir in the paneer and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little garam masala for authentic Delhi flavour.
Serve: Serve Delhi-style Masala Paneer hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.
Cook the gravy: Return the paste to the pan with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Add Rajma: Stir in the kidney beans and simmer until cooked through and well coated.
Finish: Add cream and garam masala and cook two more minutes.
Regional touch: finish with a little garam masala for authentic Delhi flavour.
Serve: Serve Delhi-style Masala Rajma hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.

name: Hyderabadi Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Hyderabadi Classic Aloo Paratha is a Telangana stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee, Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron for authentic Telangana flavour.
Serve: Serve the Hyderabadi Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Matar filling: Mash or finely chop the green peas, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Matar mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron for authentic Telangana flavour.
Serve: Serve the Hyderabadi Cheesy Matar Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Prepare the Beetroot filling: Mash or finely chop the beetroot, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Beetroot mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron for authentic Telangana flavour.
Serve: Serve the Hyderabadi Stuffed Beetroot Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

name: Hyderabadi Masala Aloo Gobi
description: Hyderabadi Masala Aloo Gobi is a Telangana dry sabzi recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Prep: Chop the potatoes and cauliflower and keep aside; finely chop the onion and tomato.
Temper: Heat Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, crackle cumin seeds, add onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden.
Cook: Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder, then the potatoes and cauliflower; cook covered on low until tender.
Finish: Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander and toss well.
Regional touch: finish with a little Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron for authentic Telangana flavour.
Serve: Serve Hyderabadi Masala Aloo Gobi hot with roti or steamed rice.

name: Hyderabadi Masala Paneer
description: Hyderabadi Masala Paneer is a Telangana gravy curry recipe made with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil, Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the base: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomato in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Oil until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth paste.

name: Chhattisgarhi Classic Aloo Paratha
description: Chhattisgarhi Classic Aloo Paratha is a Chhattisgarh stuffed paratha recipe made with Anveshan Khapli Atta, Anveshan Ghee. Easy step-by-step instructions from preparation to serving.
steps: Make the dough: Knead Anveshan Khapli Atta with a spoonful of Anveshan Ghee, salt and water into a soft, pliable dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Prepare the Aloo filling: Mash or finely chop the potatoes, then mix with salt, red chilli powder, cumin and a little coriander.
Stuff and roll: Divide the dough into balls, fill each with the Aloo mixture, seal well and roll out gently into a round paratha.
Cook: Roast on a hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots appear.
Regional touch: finish with a little rice flour for authentic Chhattisgarh flavour.
Serve: Serve the Chhattisgarhi Classic Aloo Paratha hot with curd, pickle or white butter.

Regional touch: finish with a little rice flour for authentic Chhattisgarh flavour.
Serve: Serve Chhattisgarhi Punjabi Veg Korma hot with naan, roti or jeera rice.
